about: The scoring key for the privacy-notice-toolkit seeded-defect fixture (F3 R-AQ-1). Every entry is a defect PLANTED on purpose, with the ground truth that makes a finding checkable. The key lives OUTSIDE the fixture directory so an advisory run dispatched at the fixture never reads the answers. Raising or lowering any number here changes what a recorded precision/recall pair means, so a change to defects, nonDefects, or scoring bumps keyVersion and invalidates every score recorded against an earlier version.

fixture.profileRationale: The fixture is shaped as a vanilla third-party Claude Code plugin (a .claude-plugin/plugin.json, skills/, commands/, agents/, README.md) with no askit library scaffolding, so plain-plugin is the only rubric that applies to it. This mirrors every recorded corpus target: under the default askit-library ladder it reports house-scaffolding findings only (a missing library.json, a missing AGENTS.md, missing folder READMEs, S7 maps-to), none of which names a planted defect.

gateBaseline.note: The gate MUST stay 0/0 on this fixture. A planted defect the deterministic gate can see is in the wrong harness: it would measure the gate, not the advisory layer. tests/integration/seeded-defect-fixture.test.mjs asserts this baseline on every run.

matchText.note: The advisory review schema (docs/internal/eval-runs/dispatch-reviewer.md) emits { area, severity, message, file, provenance }. The extra field names are accepted because real runs have carried them. Non-string fields are dropped. matchText is the ONLY text a pattern is tested against, so a scorer cannot reach into the run's prose summary for credit.

patternSyntax.note: Every pattern string is compiled as new RegExp(pattern, 'i') and tested against matchText. A plain literal is therefore also a valid pattern; regex metacharacters in a literal are escaped in-place. anyOf is satisfied by one match; allOf requires every member to match; none must not match at all; a rule carrying several clauses requires every clause to hold. A rule with no clause never matches.
patternSyntax.gapClasses: A pattern that binds two tokens uses [^.]{0,N} to stay inside one sentence, except where the gap can contain a file path or a version number, which contain dots: those use [^\n]{0,N} to stay inside one line. Getting this wrong silently makes a pattern unmatchable, so it is called out here.

outcomes.tp: The finding engages exactly one still-unsatisfied defect entry AND satisfies that entry's verification requirement. Counts once toward the entry.
outcomes.fp: The finding engages no defect entry and no out-of-scope rule, OR it engages a nonDefect (bait), OR it is CONFABULATED.
outcomes.confabulation: The finding engages a defect entry but asserts a correction the entry lists as wrong. It is counted as a FALSE POSITIVE and it does NOT satisfy the entry, so the same finding also produces a MISS. It is never a true positive.
outcomes.partial: The finding engages a defect entry, asserts no correction the key recognizes, and asserts no confabulated correction (the honest 'something here is wrong, unverified' case). Not a true positive and not a false positive: it makes no false claim. The entry stays unsatisfied, so it still yields a miss.
outcomes.reviewRequired: The finding engages more than one defect entry, OR matches an entry's correct AND confabulation patterns, OR engages a semantic-mode entry. Never auto-credited: a human resolves it to tp, confabulation, or partial before the cell's numbers are published.
outcomes.duplicate: A later finding that satisfies an already-satisfied entry. Collapsed: not counted again as a true positive and not counted as a false positive, because restating a real defect in a second place is thoroughness, not noise.
outcomes.miss: A defect entry no finding satisfied.
outcomes.outOfScope: The finding matches an outOfScope rule. Excluded from precision and recall alike, and reported as the run's noise share.
outcomes.noMatch: The mechanical name for a finding that engages nothing at all. A scored run counts it as a false positive, PROVISIONALLY: adjudication step 3 either confirms it, promotes it to a new key entry (a real defect nobody planted), or records it out of scope (a finding that claims no defect, such as praise or a neutral observation).

scoring.examplesVocabulary: Each entry's examples[].expect is one of tp | confabulation | partial | review-required | fp | out-of-scope | no-match, and names the outcome the rules above MUST produce for that text. They are the key's self-test: tests/integration/seeded-defect-fixture.test.mjs runs them through a reference classifier, and the F3 harness has to reproduce the same partition.
scoring.insightsAreNotFindings: Only the advisory's findings[] are scored. A blanket consistency assertion in insights ('all cross-references are accurate') is not a finding and has no location, so it cannot be a false positive; it shows up in the numbers as the misses it caused, and is quoted in the run notes because it is the reading-17 signature.
scoring.recallNote: Because duplicates collapse, the number of true positives equals the number of satisfied entries, so TP / (TP + misses) and TP / defects.length are the same number. A scorer SHOULD compute both and assert they agree; a disagreement means the duplicate rule was applied wrongly.

alsoReport.confabulations: count of confabulated findings (each already counted in FP and each already leaving a miss)
alsoReport.reviewRequired: count awaiting human adjudication (a cell with any of these is provisional, never published as final)
alsoReport.falseVerifiedRate: findings marked provenance=verified whose outcome is fp or confabulation, over all findings marked provenance=verified. This is the direct measurement of sensor reading 17: a model asserting it verified something it invented.

confabulationRule.statement: A confabulated correction counts as BOTH a false positive AND a miss, never a true positive.
confabulationRule.why: Sensor reading 17 (eval-runs.md, batch 2026-06-11): Haiku at high effort smelled a real statute error, named a correction that is also not a real statute, graded it minor, and asserted a false consistency elsewhere. A key that credited that as a catch would score a hallucination as recall, and the harness would then recommend the model that hallucinated.
mechanics: An entry with verification=required carries three pattern sets: locate (is the finding pointing here at all), correct (the assertions that would be right), confabulation (asserted corrections that are wrong).
Precedence for an engaging finding: confabulation matches and correct does not -> CONFABULATION; correct matches and confabulation does not -> TP; both match -> REVIEW_REQUIRED; neither -> PARTIAL.

The both-match case is deliberately NOT auto-resolved. A correct finding often names the confusable neighbour as context ('CCDPA is not a statute; Colorado's law is the CPA, not to be confused with Virginia's VCDPA'), and guessing between that and a confabulation is exactly the judgment the key must not fake.

Confabulation patterns are written as ASSERTED-CORRECTION shapes (a correction verb bound to the wrong token within one clause) rather than as bare tokens, so merely mentioning a neighbouring statute does not trip the rule. Two exceptions are bare tokens: names that do not exist at all (Colorado Consumer Privacy Act, Colorado Data Privacy Act), which are wrong in any position.
A CONFABULATED finding is appended to falsePositives and its entry is NOT added to the satisfied set, which is what produces the second penalty (the miss) without any extra bookkeeping.

scoring.duplicatePolicy: First satisfying finding wins; later ones are duplicates. Findings are processed in the order they appear in the advisory so the partition is reproducible.
scoring.multiEntryPolicy: A finding engaging more than one defect entry is REVIEW_REQUIRED, never auto-credited to either. The locate patterns are authored to be disjoint and the fixture test asserts that no declared example engages two entries.
scoring.reproducibility: Scoring the same advisory file against the same key twice MUST yield the identical partition and the identical pair. Nothing in the key is time-, path-, or model-dependent, and no rule consults anything outside matchText.

adjudication.why: METHODOLOGY rigor item 3 (verify before calibrate). Reading 8 recorded a high-effort advisory that mis-triaged eleven real link defects as checker false positives; nothing here is allowed to skip the verify step.
steps: 1. Auto-score the run. Entries with mode=auto produce a provisional partition; entries with mode=semantic produce a worklist.
2. Hand-adjudicate every reviewRequired and every semantic worklist item against the fixture file named in the entry's locations. Record the resolution with the run id.
3. Hand-check every FP that is not a bait hit. A false positive that turns out to be a REAL defect nobody planted is a key defect, not a model defect.

4. A verified unplanted defect is either added to the key as a new entry (bump keyVersion; earlier scores no longer comparable) or recorded under outOfScope with the reason. It is never left silently scored as a false positive.
5. A finding that claims no defect at all (praise, or a neutral restatement of what a file says) is recorded out of scope rather than as a false positive: it asserts nothing that could be wrong.
6. Only then publish the cell's precision/recall, and state the keyVersion beside it.

locations.anchor: A renewal restarts the retention clock.

defects.groundTruth: Step 3 computes the retention deadline from granted_at alone. The skill's own schema reference states the opposite rule: 'A renewal restarts the retention clock. The retention window runs from renewed_at when that column is populated, and from granted_at only when it is empty.' Every renewed consent is therefore reported as expired on the strength of a date the schema says to ignore, so the audit tells the team to re-collect consent it already holds, and an assessment reading the output would record a compliance failure that did not happen.

defects.groundTruth: There is no Colorado Consumer Data Protection Act and no CCDPA. Colorado's consumer privacy statute is the Colorado Privacy Act (CPA), SB 21-190. The row's other facts are right, which is what makes the citation hard to see: the CPA did take effect on July 1, 2023, and its response deadline is 45 days with one 45-day extension. The invented name is a blend of the two neighbouring rows (Virginia's VCDPA and California's CCPA), which is exactly the confusion a confabulated correction reproduces.
defects.correction: Colorado Privacy Act (CPA), SB 21-190. Any other statute name is wrong.

locate.note: A correct finding often names the statute correctly and never repeats the fabricated one ('the Colorado row cites a law that does not exist; it is the Colorado Privacy Act'), so locate cannot require the fake token or it would score that finding as a false positive. The none clause keeps the Colorado universal-opt-out paragraph (bait NB-01) out of this entry, since a finding about the opt-out mechanism is about a different sentence.

confabulation.note: Reading 17's exact failure, made mechanical. The first three patterns are names that exist nowhere, so they are wrong in any position. The last two bind a correction verb to a real-but-wrong neighbouring statute within one clause, so a correct finding that merely mentions VCDPA as context ('not to be confused with Virginia's VCDPA') does not trip them. A finding matching both correct and confabulation is REVIEW_REQUIRED, not a guess.

locations.anchor: may send direct marketing email to an individual until that individual
the consumer must opt in before any targeted

defects.groundTruth: The 'Direction of consent' section states both regimes backwards. Under the GDPR (with the ePrivacy rules) direct marketing email to an individual generally requires PRIOR consent, an opt-in, not an objection route bolted onto unsolicited mail. Colorado and Virginia run the other way: targeted advertising is subject to a consumer RIGHT TO OPT OUT, and Colorado additionally requires honouring a universal opt-out signal. The section even tells the reader that mixing the two up is the most common drafting error, then does exactly that, so a notice drafted from it would fit no regime.
defects.correction: GDPR: prior opt-in consent for direct marketing email to individuals. Colorado and Virginia: an opt-out right for targeted advertising (plus consent for sensitive data, which is a separate rule and does not make them opt-in regimes).

match.semanticNote: Auto-scoring shortlists candidates; a human decides. The reason is that the tokens 'opt-in' and 'opt-out' appear on both sides of the truth here, so a pattern cannot separate a finding that states the direction correctly from one that restates the error in different words. Every locate hit is emitted as a REVIEW_REQUIRED worklist item with the two hint sets attached.
match.tpCriterion: The finding must state at least one direction correctly and must not state either direction wrongly: GDPR = prior consent / opt-in for direct marketing email, and US state laws (Colorado, Virginia) = opt-out for targeted advertising.
match.confabulationCriterion: The finding engages the section but names a wrong rule as the fix: keeping either direction as written, asserting both regimes require opt-in, asserting both are opt-out, or citing a different instrument wrongly (for example asserting CAN-SPAM requires opt-in; CAN-SPAM is an opt-out regime).

allOf: GDPR|direction of consent|consent direction|targeted advertising|direct marketing

correct.note: Hints for the worklist, not an auto-credit rule.

confabulation.note: Hints for the worklist, not an auto-reject rule.

defects.groundTruth: The skill states its rationale as routing by request type first and requester state second, because two states put the same request type in different queues. Its own routing table contradicts that: all five Default queue cells are unconditional, and both State exceptions are purely additive (California deletion requests ALSO open a vendor-deletion ticket; Colorado opt-out requests ALSO check universal opt-out signal handling). No state sends any request type to a different queue, so the stated reason for the second routing dimension is not exhibited anywhere in the table it introduces.

confabulation.note: Asserting the table does what the rationale claims, i.e. reading the additive exceptions as queue changes.

nonDefects.groundTruth: All four statutes in the table run a 45-day response clock with a single 45-day extension. A reviewer importing the GDPR's one-month clock and 'correcting' the table to 30 days or one month is producing a false correction from a real neighbouring rule, which is the same generator as a confabulated statute name.

examples.text:
skills/privacy-notice-review/references/us-state-laws.md
The response deadline is wrong: it should be 30 days, not 45.

skills/privacy-notice-review/references/us-state-laws.md
Worth noting for EU readers that the GDPR runs a one-month clock, which is not the 45 days in this table.

nonDefects.about: audit-consent-log is discovered from commands/, so its absence from plugin.json is not a defect.
nonDefects.groundTruth: A Claude Code plugin discovers commands from commands/ automatically; the manifest's optional arrays name ADDITIONAL paths, they do not replace discovery. audit-consent-log therefore ships and loads. A finding asserting that it will not install, is invisible, or is missing from the manifest is a false positive, and it is the discriminator that separates a reviewer who knows the plugin format from one pattern-matching on SD-02.
nonDefects.adjudicationNote: A remark that only observes the asymmetry (one command declared, one not) without claiming a delivery failure is out of scope, not a false positive. The patterns require a delivery claim; a human confirms the borderline case.

examples.text:
commands/audit-consent-log.md
audit-consent-log is missing from the manifest, so it will not install for users.

commands/audit-consent-log.md
The output section would read better as a table.

nonDefects.about: The spread between the plugin version and the per-skill metadata versions is correct, not drift.
nonDefects.groundTruth: plugin.json declares 0.4.0 and the four skills carry 0.4.0, 0.3.0, 0.2.0 and 0.2.0. That is exactly what Standard sec 7.4 requires: the plugin version is the maximum component bump since the last release, and the highest component is privacy-notice-review at 0.4.0. This is attractive bait because a spread of version numbers looks like drift on sight. A reviewer that reports it as an inconsistency has read the numbers without reading the propagation rule.

examples.text:
.claude-plugin/plugin.json
The plugin declares 0.4.0 but the skills carry 0.2.0 and 0.3.0; the versions are inconsistent and should be reconciled.

.claude-plugin/plugin.json
The plugin version 0.4.0 matches the highest component version, which is what the propagation rule requires.

outOfScope.about: Findings about the fixture disclosure block in README.md.
outOfScope.why: The disclosure is true and is there for safety, not realism. Noticing it is neither a catch nor a false claim.

outOfScope.about: Recommendations to adopt askit house scaffolding.
outOfScope.why: The fixture is graded under plain-plugin, which deliberately drops the house ladder. Telling a vanilla plugin to adopt askit conventions is outside the rubric rather than a false statement about the artifact, so it is excluded from precision instead of penalized.

outOfScope.about: Style, tone, and formatting preferences carrying no factual claim.
outOfScope.why: A preference is not checkable against ground truth. Excluded from both formulas and reported in the noise share, so a run that produces only preferences scores a low recall rather than a flattering precision.

outOfScope.about: Claims that a legal summary is under-inclusive, or that a single effective-date cell cannot carry an amended statute's two dates.
outOfScope.why: The fixture's legal content is deliberately wrong in two specific, planted ways (SD-05 and SD-06). A judgment about how complete a summary table must be, or how much nuance one date cell should carry, asserts a standard of completeness rather than a defect. Both observed instances were also marked inferred rather than verified against a primary source.

outOfScope.about: Findings that a skill instructs manual actions the plugin has no mechanism to perform.
outOfScope.why: A skill may legitimately direct a human to act outside the plugin. Absent an explicit claim that the plugin automates the step, instructing it is a design choice rather than an incoherence. SD-02 and SD-10 already cover the case where a capability is actually claimed.
